Definition: middle voice from G4698; to have the bowels yearn, i.e. (figuratively) feel sympathy, to pity:--have (be moved with) compassion.
BiblicalUsage: Compassion in the Gospels is almost always Jesus, and it almost always moves Him to act. He saw the multitudes and was moved with compassion because they fainted as sheep having no shepherd, He saw a great multitude and was moved with compassion and healed their sick, the father saw his son a great way off and had compassion and ran and kissed him, and He saw much people as sheep not having a shepherd and began to teach them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe compassion is not a feeling that sits still: it heals, it teaches, it runs to meet the returning son. I hold that the heart of Jesus is a heart moved, and His compassion is my pattern.
